arm_rule: upworthy.headline_arms without its outcome-dependent filters: one arm per distinct headline_key per test, ordered by first package time then text, arm_id = test_id:arm_idx, tests with >= 2 arms. Checked 2026-10-20 on the 11,969 non-holdout tests: the text-only rule reproduces the loaders' 53,181 arm ids and headlines exactly. Any Stage 9 holdout item whose arm id or text differs fails closed

arm_set_rule.why: the text-only rebuild uses ALL packages; the single outcome read (upworthy.load_packages) drops zero-impression and exact-duplicate packages. A holdout arm whose packages all had zero impressions (or a test left with fewer than 2 arms, or arms re-ordered by a dropped first package) would give different test_id:arm_idx ids on the two sides, and sealed-run would fail closed AFTER the one outcome read
arm_set_rule.rule: an arm is identified on both sides by (test id, sha256 of its headline_key text), never by arm_idx. runner.predict binds the pre-collection's {(test id, text sha256): arm id} index (precollect.load_results arm_index, from the sealed arms.jsonl) to the holdout source BEFORE the read (runner._bind_precollection; a real holdout run without it refuses). At the read every load_packages arm is re-keyed to the pre-collection arm id with the same key (precollect.reconcile in sources.UpworthyHoldoutSource.items): pair ids, arm ids and arm refs are the pre-collection's
arm_set_rule.exclusions: pre-collection arms and tests the outcome read lacks are excluded by rule: no pair, no arm record, no outcome; their counts (n_pre/outcome/excluded tests and arms, n_excluded_arms_in_kept_tests, n_rekeyed_arms) are sealed in stage9:PREDICTIONS arm_set and printed in the report; every endpoint n counts kept arms only
arm_set_rule.coverage: the text-only side is a superset by construction (same eligible tests, same headline_key, a subset of the packages), so every table covers the outcome arms. An outcome arm with no pre-collection arm of the same key refuses (fail closed); so does any arm without its table rows
arm_set_rule.kept_values: kept arms keep their pre-collection frontier picks (a pick of an excluded arm gives the kept arms no vote, as an invalid pick does), probe answers (a probe answer naming an excluded arm leaves that test out of the probe rows; an N answer stays a not-recognised row), describes, readouts and embedding scores (voyage within-test grouping = the full text-only test). order_a/order_b (position, always-newer, b_is_later) stay the load_packages arm_idx. Frontier picks were made among all k text-only arms while Lens ranks the kept arms only, so a vote for an excluded arm is lost (more ties, split credit in F1); this is stated now and not rescored (Emily's ruling 2 of 2026-10-23: the ties stay, F1 is provisional and never gated, the disclosure stays). The pair id, and so the A/B slot coin, is built from the sorted pre-collection ids, never from the outcome-side order
arm_set_rule.null_pairs: the spec 4.7 constructed null pairs are the staged ones (null_pairs.jsonl: nulls.null_specs on the pre-collection text set), loaded before the read by frozen_models.FrozenStack.null_items, their texts taken from the voyage stage's texts.jsonl (sha256 = the sealed stage9_emb:UPLOAD upload_sha256). This is a named non-source access (data_flow.non_source_accesses.sealed_run_null_texts, Emily's ruling 3 of 2026-10-23): a sealed-file access checked against its sha256, not a read of the holdout source, so it is not counted in data_flow.reads

spend_rule.ruling: Hemant (owner) in chat on 2026-10-23, option A: limit by actual spend
spend_rule.rule: submit in chunks of at most 5,000 requests, in the sealed chunk order, one chunk at a time. Before each chunk: actual spend so far + that chunk's EXPECTED cost must be <= 68 USD; if not, nothing is submitted and stage9_pre:STOPPED is sealed (chunk, requests submitted, actual, next expected, cap). After each chunk: collect it, seal every result and its actual spend (stage9_pre:SPEND:<batch>), then decide the next chunk; submit refuses while a submitted chunk is uncollected
spend_rule.actual_spend: measured from the collected batch results: per succeeded result input tokens x the pinned input price + output tokens x the pinned output price (a non-zero cache token count fails closed) (precollect.PRICES: Opus 5.5 2/10, Sonnet 5.5 1/5 USD per M tokens, Batch = 50% of the standard 4/20 and 2/10, checked 2026-10-23 against the claude-api pricing reference); errored or expired results count 0 (not billed); a result naming an unpriced model or without token counts fails closed; each parsed file must equal the sha256 sealed in its SPEND entry
spend_rule.expected_model: precollect.EXPECTED_USD, the per-request model behind the 34 USD figure (READINESS_2026-10-20 section 2): describe 0.001561 USD (describe_ext/COST.json, 4,861 calibrated Opus describes); Opus pick or probe 179 input + 81 output tokens = 0.001168 USD; Sonnet pick or probe 5.41 USD / 21,774 = 0.000248 USD (the 8.1 actual). Each chunk's expected cost is sealed in the build's chunk_plan and re-computed at submit
spend_rule.credit: credit in hand >= the 70 USD reserve at build (before the holdout read) and at the first chunk; >= the chunk's expected cost at every chunk; the prepaid credit is the hard ceiling (no card on file)
spend_rule.worst_case: computed per request (precollect.worst_usd) and per chunk, sealed in stage9_pre:BUILD (worst_usd, chunk_plan) as information only; it no longer refuses submit
spend_rule.recording: review of PR #125: the sealed ledger is the record, state.json only a copy. Before each create an INTENT entry is sealed (stage9_pre:INTENT:<chunk>:<attempt>), the create is made with max_retries=0 and the SUBMIT entry is sealed right after it. Before every submit and every run step the account's batch list is read (client.messages.batches.list) and any batch created since the build (15 minute margin) that is not a sealed SUBMIT entry refuses: a billed batch is never left unrecorded and never followed by a second one. Actual spend is the sum of the sealed SPEND entries, each re-computed from its parsed file
spend_rule.collect: a batch's results must be exactly its chunk's sealed custom ids (index rows first..first+n): once each, none missing, no extra, else nothing is sealed and the chunk stays uncollected, so the next submit stays blocked. The parsed file is written atomically before the COMMIT of the results and the SPEND entry; a chunk whose SPEND entry exists and matches its file counts as collected (crash recovery). A non-zero cache token count fails closed (no request sets cache_control)

chunk_order_rule.rule: requests are grouped by holdout test: the test's describes (custom id order), then per frontier arm (Opus, then Sonnet) its fwd pick, rev pick and recognition probe if the test is a probe test; tests are ordered by sha256('lens.stage9.chunk_order/1|' + test id); whole tests are packed greedily into chunks of at most 5,000 requests. requests.jsonl and index.jsonl are written in this order and the plan (first, n, n_tests, n_by_kind, expected_usd, worst_usd per chunk) is sealed in stage9_pre:BUILD
chunk_order_rule.why: fair interleave fixed before the re-build: every chunk carries the describes of its tests' pairs and both frontier arms' picks of the same tests, in a test order no one chose, so a stop leaves a random subset of whole tests covered by every feature, never one feature without another and never half a test

partial_rule.seal: seal-results seals a STOPPED run's collected chunks (complete false, stopped true); the submitted chunks must be the first chunks of the sealed plan and match the STOPPED count, else load fails closed
partial_rule.describes: a describe never sent is a missing describe: toward_y None in describe.jsonl, which the stack reads as its missing-describe indicator (m = 1), exactly as a failed describe call
partial_rule.frontier: each frontier arm scores the tests whose fwd and rev picks were sent and reports n covered (load_results coverage, sealed as precollect_coverage in stage9:PREDICTIONS; F1 n_tests); arms of tests never sent carry no frontier score and their probe rows are absent; F1 runs on the covered tests only
partial_rule.fail_closed: a request that was sent and has no sealed result, a result for a request never sent, a missing score inside a covered test, or a missing score in a complete run still refuses

supersedes.what: the first Stage 9 seal of 2026-10-23, superseded before any paid call or outcome read because the worst-case cap blocked submission
supersedes.holdout_text_reads: that build read the holdout text once (read 0 in `what`); the re-build reads it once more (read 1), so the count goes from 4 to 5
supersedes.ledgers: archived, not deleted: both ledgers and the first build's files move to engine/experiments/stage9/_archive/2026-10-23_first_seal/ before the re-seal
supersedes.seal_config_guard: publication.require_published refuses a package whose sha256 is listed in supersedes.package, so the v2 config cannot be sealed against v1
